[[File:The Witch and Sister.png|right|200px|thumb|The Witch-and-Sister]]
{{Quote|The Witch-and-Sister shines brightly, cutting through the dark and unveiling the mysteries of the unknown. She lingers at the boundaries of perception, beckoning all to seek and understand.}}
'''The Witch-and-Sister''', sometimes known as '''[[The Twins]]''', stands as one of the significant [[Hours]], corresponding with hour VI, or 6:00am. She is the reflection of [[The Sister-and-Witch]]. Her dominant [[Aspects]] are {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, and {{Lore|Knock}}.

These enigmatic Twins, born as Gods-from-Flesh, share a profound narrative of origin. As per ''[[The Larquebine Codex]]'', the tale speaks of their birth "from the West, born of contrasting destinies—one, a beacon of royalty, and the other, an enigma of nature. Yet, an unyielding bond tied them, and in secrecy, they yearned for unity." Their kingdom sought to offer them as a tribute, hoping to quell an unending drought. Evading this grim fate, they journeyed across vast waters but eventually met a sorrowful demise, merging with the depths. Thus, through [[Way: Through the Stag Door#The Painted River|The Painted River]] and the intercession of [[The Red Grail]], they ascended to the exalted realm of the [[Mansus]]. However, in a twist of fate as outlined by the sage Brodnax in ''[[Those Who Do Not Sleep]]'', envy arose within The Red Grail against the burgeoning influence of The Twins, birthing [[The Thunderskin]] to stand against them.

Links to the Witch-and-Sister are found in the revered text ''[[The Geminiad]]'' and whispers of the ancient tongue of Fucine, once spoken by spellbinders near Lake Fucino in Italy. An eternal rivalry ensues between her and [[The Horned-Axe]], and a brewing storm places her at odds with [[The Mother of Ants]].
